summary:
v2 ATR flip executed through a native-OCO handoff, plus a stale-ask guard on buy-stop placement. Second head; all three of my findings on 6b5e912 are closed. Base is current origin/main; ONE commit; commit_agent() returns codex-2 so the reviewer differs from the author.

THE DEFECT THIS FIXES IS LIVE AND MEASURED. On 2026-09-08 NUR flipped short and CW_FLIP fired at 13:29:47 on both legs. Webull obeyed and exited at 3.19; the Schwab leg's release came back COULD_NOT_TELL and _evaluate_v2_managed_exit returned on the native-OCO stand-down before consulting the pending flip, so no exit was sent. Schwab rode from 3.24 to 3.07 on its OCO stop five minutes later -- about $0.24 worse on 2 shares than the flip price. This PR is what lets the Schwab leg act on a decision the strategy had already made.

⛔ IT RELEASES BROKER-SIDE PROTECTION ON A LIVE POSITION, so the review weight is on the failure branches, not the happy path. They are right:
- Only "released" proceeds to a close. "unanswerable" logs OMS-V2-CW-FLIP-REFUSED, keeps the bracket and submits NO sell.
- "resolved_by_fill" closes bookkeeping only, with no second sell.
- The one-shot flip latch is claimed BEFORE broker I/O (_cw_flip_release_inflight) and _cw_flip_pending is popped before the await, with CancelledError restoring it, so two quote tasks cannot cancel one bracket or submit two closes.
- The decision is bound to the managed-position UUID at the release-target read AND again at the emit via expected_managed_row_id.
- No speculative retry and no re-protection loop was added, which is correct: re-protecting on a refused close is how a third sell lands against the same shares.

MY THREE FINDINGS ON THE PREVIOUS HEAD, EACH RE-VERIFIED CLOSED BY MY OWN MUTATION:
1. AUTHORSHIP. Both prior commits carried Co-Authored-By: Claude and no Codex trailer, so the gate attributed them to claude-1 and a claude-1 pin was mechanically impossible. Re-checked with the gate's own commit_agent() rather than by eye: the single commit now returns codex-2.
2. THE UNCOVERED STATE REACHED NOBODY. OMS-V2-CW-FLIP-UNCOVERED was an ERROR log consumed by nothing -- not ops/, not a health check, not an incident -- in a file that already had _raise_webull_handle_lost_incident for the same class. It now writes a CRITICAL SystemIncident, status=open, titled "CW flip UNCOVERED: <symbol> on <account>; close or protect now", carrying account, symbol, managed row, release state and close outcome, on the surface the control plane already reads.
   MY MUTATION: remove the incident write while KEEPING the ERROR log -> test_cw_flip_reports_uncovered_when_close_fails_after_oco_release RED. That is the distinction I asked for: it separates a visible report from a log-only claim, and a log line is not a channel to the operator. Today's own record is why -- SIL1's alarm had never once fired in its life and the D6 watchdog sat RED since Saturday with nobody reading it.
3. THE MANAGED-ROW BINDING WAS UNCOVERED. On the previous head I mutated `row is None or str(row.id) != expected_row_id` to `row is None` TARGETED INSIDE _release_native_oco_for_cw_flip and got 27 passed -- GREEN. The same targeted mutation on this head turns test_cw_flip_refuses_release_if_position_changes_before_target_read RED. The control replaces position A with B immediately before the target read and asserts different_position, no broker release, no sell, B still open. The UUID conjunct is now proven to prevent touching a replacement's bracket.

STILL RED, RE-CONFIRMED ON THIS HEAD:
- sell even when the release is UNANSWERABLE -> test_cw_flip_never_sells_when_native_oco_release_is_unanswerable RED. This is the one that matters most: it is what stops a sell going out against a bracket we could not prove was cancelled.
- accept a stale ask -> 2 RED, first-slot AND reclaim independently.
Each mutant parse-checked before running; tree restored clean at 85/85.

THE STALE-ASK FIX IS CORRECT AND ANSWERS A MEASURED CASE. MOBX 13:16:02 was rejected by Schwab with the broker's own words: "The stop price must be above the current ask for buy stop orders and below the bid for sell stop orders." We had sent a buy-stop at 1.30 off a 17-second-old ask while the live ask had already crossed it; Webull filled at 1.30 eleven seconds later, confirming where the market was. That was OUR malformed order, not the broker declining, and it belongs to the "OURS, not the broker's" class that was 7% of live refusals in the 2026-09-08 census. A present quote must now be under 10s old before its ask can authorise placement.
⭐ A WHOLLY ABSENT QUOTE RETAINS FAIL-OPEN, AND THAT IS RIGHT: an absent quote and a stale quote are different epistemic states, and the broker remains the backstop for the first. The bound is a setting, which it should be.

CONTROLLED PAIR, one variable, same command, pristine worktrees nothing touched during the run: base 5862b89 46 failed / 3371 passed / 12 errors; head 43372c6 46 failed / 3380 passed / 12 errors. +9 is exactly the nine new tests. Failure sets AND error sets extracted and diffed BY NAME: IDENTICAL. codex-2 reported 55/3330 -> 55/3339 on its platform, the same +9 with the known environment gap recorded on earlier pins.
⛔ I did NOT run this pair on the previous head and said so at the time; it is run here.

NOT COVERED, and none of it blocks:
(a) UNEXERCISED. No live ATR flip has yet run through this path. The NUR case is why it exists, not evidence that it works.
(b) The filled Webull claim that outlived its closed position is deliberately unchanged and needs an operator policy decision. MOBX 13:35 was suppressed by a claim 1,174,975 ms old whose position had closed ~3 minutes earlier; that is a separate row.
(c) The 2-vs-1 fan-out size asymmetry is untraced and unrelated to this change.
⛔ A PIN IS NOT DEPLOY AUTHORIZATION. This touches the live exit path, the box is still on 5de2c363, and a position is open.
